SeekDesk local compatibility changes
===================================

Base: liquid_glass_widgets 1.17.3, as distributed by pub.dev.
Source: https://pub.dev/packages/liquid_glass_widgets/versions/1.17.3
Repository: https://github.com/sdegenaar/liquid_glass_widgets
License: MIT; see LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES in this directory.

This directory contains the original runtime library, shaders, iOS plugin,
package metadata and license documents. Examples and upstream test fixtures are
not required to build SeekDesk and are omitted. upstream-manifest.json records
the SHA-256 of each original file before any local modification.

SeekDesk keeps the upstream version number to identify the base release. The
app's pubspec uses this source directory explicitly; pub-cache is not modified.

Local patch scope
-----------------

Round 27: scrollable segment geometry and interaction compatibility
  lib/src/widgets/interactive/scrollable_segment_content.dart

The scrollable segment control must track actual label geometry when titles,
text scales, font weights or the order of the same number of segments change.
The patch preserves the control instance, surviving segment identities and
official glass renderer, shaders and springs. It does not replace natural-width
tabs with fixed-width cells or rebuild the entire control on a title update.

Regression coverage lives in Flutter/test/workspace_tabs_geometry_test.dart.
It measures the public indicator against rendered cells after title/font/order
changes, viewport clamping and interrupted regrids; it also checks element and
focus identity, pointer cancellation, accessibility activation, first subsequent
lens drag, manual scroll ownership and the absence of perpetual scheduled frames.

Actual layout notifications are coalesced after layout. Viewport metrics refresh
screen-relative geometry even when ScrollPosition clamps without a listener
callback. A press whose geometry changes is invalidated for that gesture only;
stable ID lookup prevents an old cell from activating a new numeric slot.

Round 30: optional synchronous renderer work diagnostics
  lib/glass_work_diagnostics.dart (new)
  lib/src/engine/liquid_glass_layer.dart
  lib/src/engine/multi_shader_builder.dart
  lib/src/engine/render_liquid_glass_geometry.dart
  lib/src/engine/rendering/liquid_glass_render_object.dart

The new diagnostic API is imported explicitly by SeekDesk; the package's public
barrel exports are unchanged. Both SEEKDESK_PROFILE_FRAMES and
SEEKDESK_PROFILE_RAW_FRAMES must be enabled at compile time, and an observer must
be installed before measurements are created. The normal application leaves
these flags disabled.

Instrumented operations are shape-geometry checks, geometry-picture recording,
synchronous geometry-image handle creation, shadow baking and FragmentShader
instance creation. Observations contain fixed kinds, timestamps, frame numbers,
durations, sizes and counts; no application text or file/network I/O is added.
Observer errors are contained and must not replace a renderer exception.

These are timing hooks, not rendering-algorithm changes: cache conditions,
geometry invalidation, shader code, rendering order and quality selection are
preserved. Shape-geometry observations include cache checks; they are not a
count of actual rebuilds. Synchronous image-handle creation does not measure GPU
completion, and these scopes do not measure every rendering operation.
Regression coverage lives in Flutter/test/glass_work_diagnostics_test.dart.

Round 31: retain fixed segmented-control labels during spring ticks
  lib/src/widgets/interactive/segmented_control_internal.dart

The ordinary label subtree is passed through VelocitySpringBuilder.child and
then SpringBuilder.child. Alignment-spring ticks no longer reconstruct that
subtree. Parent/configuration updates still create current labels, and the
active-lens foreground-color branch continues to update when required. Indicator
alignment, velocity, thickness, paint-pass order, semantics and interaction
callbacks retain their existing implementation. No cross-configuration label
cache or notifier-lifecycle change is introduced.

Regression coverage lives in Flutter/test/glass_segmented_animation_test.dart:
retained labels while the indicator moves, implicit/explicit lens contrast,
changed labels and callbacks, disabled and semantic activation, theme/text scale,
RTL/direction/size changes, and item-count changes with hover/focus interaction.

Round 32: retain button animation and focus-region lifecycle state
  lib/widgets/interactive/glass_button.dart
  lib/widgets/shared/glass_focus_region.dart

Transparent buttons retain a stable opacity wrapper when enabled changes, so
their stretch/glow elements and spring state survive edit/preview transitions.
Filled and prominent buttons retain their original wrapper structure: even an
opacity of one is a shared-backdrop boundary. Disabling a button clears any
unfinished ambient press highlight without changing animation or spring tuning.

Focus regions explicitly own or borrow their focus nodes and notifiers, rebind
replacements, and retire old callbacks across node and mode changes. Interactive
focus highlights follow the current node and global highlight mode rather than
a retained detector's stale focus cache. Highlight publication during build is
coalesced after the frame and targets only the current live notifiers. Regions
with a shape retain their child in a stable Stack with passthrough constraints,
preserving child state and layout while the focus ring appears or disappears.

Regression coverage lives in Flutter/test/glass_button_lifecycle_test.dart and
Flutter/test/glass_focus_region_lifecycle_test.dart: animation identity across
enabled changes, disabled pointer/keyboard/semantic activation, press/drag
release and cancellation, focus-node/notifier ownership and replacement, stale
callbacks, observed/interactive mode changes, editable selection retention and
tight-constraint child geometry when the focus ring toggles.

Round 33: retain the focus action wrapper across enabled changes
  lib/widgets/shared/glass_focus_region.dart

A stable Actions widget now wraps FocusableActionDetector. Its local action map
is supplied only when the region is enabled and can request focus; otherwise an
empty map preserves lookup of ancestor actions. The detector no longer inserts
and removes an Actions wrapper internally, avoiding GlobalKey reparenting of
its descendants when enabled changes. This preserves element state without the
previous recursive deactivate/activate and unrelated inherited-dependency work.
The detector still owns the original keyboard focus, hover and cursor behavior;
semantics, material parameters and animation controllers are unchanged.

Regression coverage lives in Flutter/test/glass_button_reparent_test.dart:
unchanged descendant lifecycle counts through enabled round trips, real theme
updates, disabled keyboard/pointer/semantic activation, and ancestor-action
fallback. Existing focus lifecycle tests invoke Actions through an attached
descendant context instead of depending on the detector's internal action map.

Across these patches, material parameters, shader assets, quality levels and
spring-physics definitions are unchanged. Round 30 modifies renderer source only
to add opt-in diagnostics; Rounds 31 through 33 change widget reuse and lifecycle
handling, not visual physics.

When updating the upstream dependency, first check whether these defects are fixed
upstream and run the geometry, lifecycle, reorder, glass interaction and optional
diagnostic tests.
Do not copy a new release over the patch without reconciling those checks.

The exact local source diff is recorded in seekdesk.patch, relative to this
directory. It contains all eight modified original runtime files and the added
glass_work_diagnostics.dart, including any formatting differences in those files.
Apply it from the package root using a patch tool with one path component removed
(-p1); additions use /dev/null as their source.

Before generating this diff, every one of the 176 original files in the local
pub-cache copy of liquid_glass_widgets 1.17.3 was checked against its SHA-256 in
upstream-manifest.json. All 176 matched. The current vendor copy retains 168 of
those files byte-for-byte, modifies eight, adds one runtime file and removes none.
An exact application of seekdesk.patch to a temporary copy of verified originals
was checked against all 177 current vendored files. The three local provenance files
(this note, seekdesk.patch and upstream-manifest.json) are excluded from the patch
itself. The original manifest is preserved unchanged. Reverify its hashes and
regenerate/replay the complete diff whenever the local patch changes.
